Lighthouse

A lighthouse is a tower with a bright light at the top that guides ships at sea. The earliest lighthouses were fires lit on hills, and later purpose built towers carried oil lamps and then lenses that concentrated the beam over long distances.

History

The Pharos of Alexandria was built in the third century BC and was counted among the seven wonders of the ancient world. Many towers followed along the Mediterranean and Atlantic coasts, each with its own character and signal pattern.
